5:54.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ مَن يَرۡتَدَّ مِنكُمۡ عَن دِينِهِۦ فَسَوۡفَ يَأۡتِي ٱللَّهُ بِقَوۡمࣲ يُحِبُّهُمۡ وَيُحِبُّونَهُۥٓ أَذِلَّةٍ عَلَى ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ أَعِزَّةٍ عَلَى ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ يُجَٰهِدُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ وَلَا يَخَافُونَ لَوۡمَةَ لَآئِمࣲۚ ذَٰلِكَ فَضۡلُ ٱللَّهِ يُؤۡتِيهِ مَن يَشَآءُۚ وَٱللَّهُ وَٰسِعٌ عَلِيمٌ
5:54.en: O ye who believe! Whoso of you becometh a renegade from his religion, (know that in his stead) Allah will bring a people whom He loveth and who love Him, humble toward believers, stern toward disbelievers, striving in the way of Allah, and fearing not the blame of any blamer. Such is the grace of Allah which He giveth unto whom He will. Allah is All-Embracing, All-Knowing

49:1.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا تُقَدِّمُواْ بَيۡنَ يَدَيِ ٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِۦۖ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمࣱ‏
49:1.en: O ye who believe! Be not forward in the presence of Allah and His messenger, and keep your duty to Allah. Lo! Allah is Hearer, Knower

61:10.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ هَلۡ أَدُلُّكُمۡ عَلَىٰ تِجَٰرَةࣲ تُنجِيكُم مِّنۡ عَذَابٍ أَلِيمࣲ‏
61:10.en: O ye who believe! Shall I show you a commerce that will save you from a painful doom

61:11.ar: تُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱللَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِۦ وَتُجَٰهِدُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ بِأَمۡوَٰلِكُمۡ وَأَنفُسِكُمۡۚ ذَٰلِكُمۡ خَيۡرࣱ لَّكُمۡ إِن كُنتُمۡ تَعۡلَمُونَ
61:11.en: Ye should believe in Allah and His messenger, and should strive for the cause of Allah with your wealth and your lives. That is better for you, if ye did but know

6:52.ar: وَلَا تَطۡرُدِ ٱلَّذِينَ يَدۡعُونَ رَبَّهُم بِٱلۡغَدَوٰةِ وَٱلۡعَشِيِّ يُرِيدُونَ وَجۡهَهُۥۖ مَا عَلَيۡكَ مِنۡ حِسَابِهِم مِّن شَيۡءࣲ وَمَا مِنۡ حِسَابِكَ عَلَيۡهِم مِّن شَيۡءࣲ فَتَطۡرُدَهُمۡ فَتَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
6:52.en: Repel not those who call upon their Lord at morn and evening, seeking His Countenance. Thou art not accountable for them in aught, nor are they accountable for thee in aught, that thou shouldst repel them and be of the wrong-doers

6:53.ar: وَكَذَٰلِكَ فَتَنَّا بَعۡضَهُم بِبَعۡضࣲ لِّيَقُولُوٓاْ أَهَٰٓؤُلَآءِ مَنَّ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡهِم مِّنۢ بَيۡنِنَآۗ أَلَيۡسَ ٱللَّهُ بِأَعۡلَمَ بِٱلشَّٰكِرِينَ
6:53.en: And even so do We try some of them by others, that they say: Are these they whom Allah favoureth among us? Is not Allah best Aware of the thanksgivers

47:38.ar: هَٰٓأَنتُمۡ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ تُدۡعَوۡنَ لِتُنفِقُواْ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ فَمِنكُم مَّن يَبۡخَلُۖ وَمَن يَبۡخَلۡ فَإِنَّمَا يَبۡخَلُ عَن نَّفۡسِهِۦۚ وَٱللَّهُ ٱلۡغَنِيُّ وَأَنتُمُ ٱلۡفُقَرَآءُۚ وَإِن تَتَوَلَّوۡاْ يَسۡتَبۡدِلۡ قَوۡمًا غَيۡرَكُمۡ ثُمَّ لَا يَكُونُوٓاْ أَمۡثَٰلَكُم
47:38.en: Lo! ye are those who are called to spend in the way of Allah, yet among you there are some who hoard. And as for him who hoardeth, he hoardeth only from his soul. And Allah is the Rich, and ye are the poor. And if ye turn away He will exchange you for some other folk, and they will not be the likes of you

6:162.ar: قُلۡ إِنَّ صَلَاتِي وَنُسُكِي وَمَحۡيَايَ وَمَمَاتِي لِلَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
6:162.en: Say: Lo! my worship and my sacrifice and my living and my dying are for Allah, Lord of the Worlds

19:59.ar: ۞فَخَلَفَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِهِمۡ خَلۡفٌ أَضَاعُواْ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَٱتَّبَعُواْ ٱلشَّهَوَٰتِۖ فَسَوۡفَ يَلۡقَوۡنَ غَيًّا
19:59.en: Now there hath succeeded them a later generation whom have ruined worship and have followed lusts. But they will meet deception

7:169.ar: فَخَلَفَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِهِمۡ خَلۡفࣱ وَرِثُواْ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ يَأۡخُذُونَ عَرَضَ هَٰذَا ٱلۡأَدۡنَىٰ وَيَقُولُونَ سَيُغۡفَرُ لَنَا وَإِن يَأۡتِهِمۡ عَرَضࣱ مِّثۡلُهُۥ يَأۡخُذُوهُۚ أَلَمۡ يُؤۡخَذۡ عَلَيۡهِم مِّيثَٰقُ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ أَن لَّا يَقُولُواْ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ إِلَّا ٱلۡحَقَّ وَدَرَسُواْ مَا فِيهِۗ وَٱلدَّارُ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةُ خَيۡرࣱ لِّلَّذِينَ يَتَّقُونَۚ أَفَلَا تَعۡقِلُونَ
7:169.en: And a generation hath succeeded them who inherited the scriptures. They grasp the goods of this low life (as the price of evil-doing) and say: It will be forgiven us. And if there came to them (again) the offer of the like, they would accept it (and would sin again). Hath not the covenant of the Scripture been taken on their behalf that they should not speak aught concerning Allah save the truth? And they have studied that which is therein. And the abode of the Hereafter is better, for those who ward off (evil). Have ye then no sense

aCbF16D8RYw.speaker: adnan
aCbF16D8RYw.speaker_note: Seventh khutbah of his own Pledge of Al-Aqabah series; same voice, structure and Arabic second khutbah as the earlier episodes.
aCbF16D8RYw.title: The Pledge of Al-Aqabah: The Fourth Article, Prioritizing the Message
aCbF16D8RYw.one_line: The fourth article of the Aqabah pledge: put Allah's message above everything, refuse compromise, and stand for Allah without fearing anyone's blame.
aCbF16D8RYw.summary: His seventh khutbah on the Pledge of Al-Aqabah takes the article in which the Ansar promised to stand up for Allah without fearing anyone's blame. He opens with Al-Ma'idah 5:54: if people turn away, Allah brings a people He loves, who love Him and do not fear the critic. Yathrib, he says, was a city with no future, torn by tribal hatred and poverty, and the Prophet came to it only once its people offered the pledge; if you want him to do for your life what he did for that city, the same commitment is required. The key is priority. Islam is the umbrella over life, not one category competing with others, and Al-Hujurat 49:1 forbids putting anything ahead of Allah and His Messenger. He asks how anyone will explain a life of 'I was too busy' to God, reads As-Saff 61:10-11 as a transaction of self and wealth, and recalls how Quraysh pressed for a small compromise to strip the message of its authenticity. In the Arabic second khutbah he says this dedication needs courage and is driven by love of Allah, built by recalling His gifts and patience. He then holds up Gaza as a test of what we really put first, and warns from Maryam 19:59 and Al-A'raf 7:169 about generations who let the message slip.

outline.heading: Opening
The people Allah loves
outline.gist: Al-Ma'idah 5:54 frames the article: if any of you turn back from the deen, Allah will bring a people He loves and who love Him, humble with believers, firm against disbelievers, striving in His way and fearing no critic's blame. He turns to the Ansar who came to Aqabah.

outline.heading: From Yathrib to the city everyone longs for
outline.gist: Madinah is now the city people around the globe would do anything to visit, where you find nothing but peace, calm and beauty. The Prophet made it that, and he went there only once its people offered him the pledge.

outline.heading: Do for your life what he did for Yathrib
outline.gist: If you want the Prophet to come into your life and do for it what he did for Yathrib, the same pledge is required. Yathrib, a name that means little to us now, was broken from the inside: its people hated each other, it was filled with poverty and its tribes fought year after year.

outline.heading: Sent to the city with no future
outline.gist: Of his many attempts to present himself to the tribes, 26 are on record, and some he did not bother to approach because he knew them. Allah sent him to a place that was not functioning, had no future and was only getting worse, so that you could see what the message does.

outline.heading: The articles of the pledge
outline.gist: He lists them: hearing and obeying in energy and reluctance, spending in hardship and ease, commanding good and forbidding wrong, and today's article, standing for Allah without fearing the blame of any critic.

outline.heading: 'Turns back': more than apostasy
outline.gist: The fourth article is staying steadfast on priority even when people criticize you for it. The verb for turning back in 5:54 is used in jurisprudence for apostasy, but it covers any lack of priority for the deen.

outline.heading: Fearless because their priority is right
outline.gist: The people Allah brings will not fear isolation or the haters' blame, because they know their priorities: Islam is the umbrella for life and everything else falls under it.

outline.heading: Islam is not a category: nothing ahead of Allah
outline.gist: Islam is not one category of life competing with others for a share of your time. Al-Hujurat 49:1 forbids putting anything at all ahead of Allah and His Messenger.

outline.heading: Why are we alive?
outline.gist: Why do I have consciousness, the ability to think deeply, make complex choices and know innately what is right and good? No other creature on the planet runs into ethical dilemmas.

outline.heading: Only one answer, and a life to explain
outline.gist: No animal lies depressed wondering whether it should have chosen differently, yet I do. There is only one answer to who put me here, and once you have it, the question is how you will explain your life and justify your choices before Allah.

outline.heading: 'I was too busy': make the argument
outline.gist: He invites anyone with a better argument to convince him how a person could tell God "I didn't have enough time, I was too busy", and make it logical. As-Saff 61:10 offers a transaction that saves from a painful punishment.

outline.heading: The transaction: wealth and self
outline.gist: Believing in Allah and His Messenger and striving with your wealth and yourselves means giving what you own inside and outside for Allah; anything less does not fulfil the purpose. That is the full commitment and priority the Prophet asked for, with no compromise.

outline.heading: Quraysh's small compromise
outline.gist: In the sixth to eighth years of his prophethood Quraysh tried to negotiate a small compromise. People who stand for nothing want you to compromise a little because it strips the halo of authenticity, originality and divinity from your faith, and he never conceded.

outline.heading: Do not drive away the weak believers
outline.gist: Al-An'am 6:52-53: do not drive away those who call on their Lord morning and evening seeking His face. The elite were tested by them, asking how Allah could favour such people over them; does Allah not know best who is grateful?

outline.heading: Take it in its totality
outline.gist: You take every aspect of the message, even where you cannot yet do all of it, commit your whole life to it and make every choice aim at getting you across the finishing line.

outline.heading: Anything less than your whole life falls short (Arabic)
outline.gist: The Prophet asked the Ansar that night to stand for Allah: devotion and sincerity, giving your life to the One who gave it. Anything less than our whole life and wealth is a real shortcoming, and Muhammad 47:38 warns that Allah can replace us with a people not like us.

outline.heading: Fearing no blame takes courage, and love
outline.gist: Do not fear anyone asking why you did it, calling it shameful or accusing you of dividing people. That needs courage, devotion, a firm hold on guidance and above all love, since no one devotes himself to someone he does not love; love of Allah is the first and last driver of this deen.

outline.heading: Recalling how patient He has been
outline.gist: Love Him by recalling how much He gave and guided you and how forbearing He was while you disobeyed and turned from His command, never expelling you from His door. Offering Him less than yourself and your wealth would be ugly character; say, as in Al-An'am 6:162, my prayer, sacrifice, life and death are for Allah.

outline.heading: Should I not be a grateful servant?
outline.gist: The Prophet stood in prayer until his feet swelled and said "should I not be a grateful servant?", and Aisha asked who could bear what he bore. The message cannot be number two in our lives.

outline.heading: Gaza: how many more children?
outline.gist: How can a billion and more Muslims not put this in its proper place of priority? How many more months, how many more children have to die, and how can anyone with a child he loves think about anything else?

outline.heading: Generations who let the message slip
outline.gist: Maryam 19:59 and Al-A'raf 7:169: successors who wasted prayer and followed desires, who inherited the Book and took the goods of this world saying "we will be forgiven". Without the priority, we will not find the beauty, ease and joy the Prophet's people found.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.note: Islam is the umbrella over life, not a category competing with others; nothing may be placed ahead of Allah and His Messenger, and the message is taken in its totality without compromise.

themes.label: Seerah events and their lessons

themes.label: Purpose, meaning and the point of life
themes.note: Human consciousness and moral struggle point to one answer about who put us here, and that answer demands a life you can justify before God.

themes.label: Accountability before Allah and goals
themes.note: 'I was too busy' and 'I didn't have enough time' are not arguments anyone can make to God.

themes.label: Courage and commitment: going all in
themes.note: Standing for Allah while people ask why you did it, call it shameful or accuse you of causing division takes courage, dedication and a firm hold on guidance.

themes.label: Love: of Allah, the Prophet, and one another
themes.note: No one dedicates himself to anyone he does not love; love of Allah is the first and last driver of the deen, built by recalling His gifts and forbearance.

themes.note: The continuing killing of children in Gaza is held up as the test of whether the ummah's priorities are right.

68:17.ar: إِنَّا بَلَوۡنَٰهُمۡ كَمَا بَلَوۡنَآ أَصۡحَٰبَ ٱلۡجَنَّةِ إِذۡ أَقۡسَمُواْ لَيَصۡرِمُنَّهَا مُصۡبِحِينَ
68:17.en: Lo! We have tried them as We tried the owners of the garden when they vowed that they would pluck its fruit next morning

68:18.en: And made no exception (for the Will of Allah)

68:19.ar: فَطَافَ عَلَيۡهَا طَآئِفࣱ مِّن رَّبِّكَ وَهُمۡ نَآئِمُونَ
68:19.en: Then a visitation from thy Lord came upon it while they slept

68:20.en: And in the morning it was as if plucked

68:21.en: And they cried out one unto another in the morning

68:22.ar: أَنِ ٱغۡدُواْ عَلَىٰ حَرۡثِكُمۡ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَٰرِمِينَ
68:22.en: Saying: Run unto your field if ye would pluck (the fruit)

68:23.en: So they went off, saying one unto another in low tones

68:24.ar: أَن لَّا يَدۡخُلَنَّهَا ٱلۡيَوۡمَ عَلَيۡكُم مِّسۡكِينࣱ‏
68:24.en: No needy man shall enter it to-day against you

68:25.en: They went betimes, strong in (this) purpose

68:26.en: But when they saw it, they said: Lo! we are in error

68:28.ar: قَالَ أَوۡسَطُهُمۡ أَلَمۡ أَقُل لَّكُمۡ لَوۡلَا تُسَبِّحُونَ
68:28.en: The best among them said: Said I not unto you: Why glorify ye not (Allah)

68:29.ar: قَالُواْ سُبۡحَٰنَ رَبِّنَآ إِنَّا كُنَّا ظَٰلِمِينَ
68:29.en: They said: Glorified be our Lord! Lo! we have been wrong-doers

68:30.en: Then some of them drew near unto others, self-reproaching

68:31.en: They said: Alas for us! In truth we were outrageous

68:32.ar: عَسَىٰ رَبُّنَآ أَن يُبۡدِلَنَا خَيۡرࣰ ا مِّنۡهَآ إِنَّآ إِلَىٰ رَبِّنَا رَٰغِبُونَ
68:32.en: It may be that our Lord will give us better than this in place thereof. Lo! we beseech our Lord

68:33.ar: كَذَٰلِكَ ٱلۡعَذَابُۖ وَلَعَذَابُ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ أَكۡبَرُۚ لَوۡ كَانُواْ يَعۡلَمُونَ
68:33.en: Such was the punishment. And verily the punishment of the Hereafter is greater if they did but know

68:34.ar: إِنَّ لِلۡمُتَّقِينَ عِندَ رَبِّهِمۡ جَنَّٰتِ ٱلنَّعِيمِ
68:34.en: Lo! for those who keep from evil are gardens of bliss with their Lord

68:1.en: Nun. By the pen and that which they write (therewith)

68:2.en: Thou art not, for thy Lord's favour unto thee, a madman

68:3.en: And lo! thine verily will be a reward unfailing

68:4.en: And lo! thou art of a tremendous nature

68:5.en: And thou wilt see and they will see

68:6.en: Which of you is the demented

68:7.ar: إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ أَعۡلَمُ بِمَن ضَلَّ عَن سَبِيلِهِۦ وَهُوَ أَعۡلَمُ بِٱلۡمُهۡتَدِينَ
68:7.en: Lo! thy Lord is Best Aware of him who strayeth from His way, and He is Best Aware of those who walk aright

68:8.en: Therefor obey not thou the rejecters

68:9.en: Who would have had thee compromise, that they may compromise

68:10.en: Neither obey thou each feeble oath-monger

68:12.en: Hinderer of the good, transgressor, malefactor

68:14.en: It is because he is possessed of wealth and children

68:15.ar: إِذَا تُتۡلَىٰ عَلَيۡهِ ءَايَٰتُنَا قَالَ أَسَٰطِيرُ ٱلۡأَوَّلِينَ
68:15.en: That, when Our revelations are recited unto him, he saith: Mere fables of the men of old

68:16.en: We shall brand him on the nose

2:264.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا تُبۡطِلُواْ صَدَقَٰتِكُم بِٱلۡمَنِّ وَٱلۡأَذَىٰ كَٱلَّذِي يُنفِقُ مَالَهُۥ رِئَآءَ ٱلنَّاسِ وَلَا يُؤۡمِنُ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡيَوۡمِ ٱلۡأٓخِرِۖ فَمَثَلُهُۥ كَمَثَلِ صَفۡوَانٍ عَلَيۡهِ تُرَابࣱ فَأَصَابَهُۥ وَابِلࣱ فَتَرَكَهُۥ صَلۡدࣰ اۖ لَّا يَقۡدِرُونَ عَلَىٰ شَيۡءࣲ مِّمَّا كَسَبُواْۗ وَٱللَّهُ لَا يَهۡدِي ٱلۡقَوۡمَ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
2:264.en: O ye who believe! Render not vain your almsgiving by reproach and injury, like him who spendeth his wealth only to be seen of men and believeth not in Allah and the Last Day. His likeness is as the likeness of a rock whereon is dust of earth; a rainstorm smiteth it, leaving it smooth and bare. They have no control of aught of that which they have gained. Allah guideth not the disbelieving folk

2:286.ar: لَا يُكَلِّفُ ٱللَّهُ نَفۡسًا إِلَّا وُسۡعَهَاۚ لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتۡ وَعَلَيۡهَا مَا ٱكۡتَسَبَتۡۗ رَبَّنَا لَا تُؤَاخِذۡنَآ إِن نَّسِينَآ أَوۡ أَخۡطَأۡنَاۚ رَبَّنَا وَلَا تَحۡمِلۡ عَلَيۡنَآ إِصۡرࣰ ا كَمَا حَمَلۡتَهُۥ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِنَاۚ رَبَّنَا وَلَا تُحَمِّلۡنَا مَا لَا طَاقَةَ لَنَا بِهِۦۖ وَٱعۡفُ عَنَّا وَٱغۡفِرۡ لَنَا وَٱرۡحَمۡنَآۚ أَنتَ مَوۡلَىٰنَا فَٱنصُرۡنَا عَلَى ٱلۡقَوۡمِ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
2:286.en: Allah tasketh not a soul beyond its scope. For it (is only) that which it hath earned, and against it (only) that which it hath deserved. Our Lord! Condemn us not if we forget, or miss the mark! Our Lord! Lay not on us such a burden as thou didst lay on those before us! Our Lord! Impose not on us that which we have not the strength to bear! Pardon us, absolve us and have mercy on us, Thou, our Protector, and give us victory over the disbelieving folk

34:31.ar: وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لَن نُّؤۡمِنَ بِهَٰذَا ٱلۡقُرۡءَانِ وَلَا بِٱلَّذِي بَيۡنَ يَدَيۡهِۗ وَلَوۡ تَرَىٰٓ إِذِ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ مَوۡقُوفُونَ عِندَ رَبِّهِمۡ يَرۡجِعُ بَعۡضُهُمۡ إِلَىٰ بَعۡضٍ ٱلۡقَوۡلَ يَقُولُ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتُضۡعِفُواْ لِلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتَكۡبَرُواْ لَوۡلَآ أَنتُمۡ لَكُنَّا مُؤۡمِنِينَ
34:31.en: And those who disbelieve say: We believe not in this Qur'an nor in that which was before it; but oh, if thou couldst see, when the wrong-doers are brought up before their Lord, how they cast the blame one to another; how those who were despised (in the earth) say unto those who were proud: But for you, we should have been believers

34:32.ar: قَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتَكۡبَرُواْ لِلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتُضۡعِفُوٓاْ أَنَحۡنُ صَدَدۡنَٰكُمۡ عَنِ ٱلۡهُدَىٰ بَعۡدَ إِذۡ جَآءَكُمۖ بَلۡ كُنتُم مُّجۡرِمِينَ
34:32.en: Those who were proud say unto those who were despised: Did we drive you away from the guidance after it had come unto you? Nay, but ye were guilty

34:33.ar: وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتُضۡعِفُواْ لِلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتَكۡبَرُواْ بَلۡ مَكۡرُ ٱلَّيۡلِ وَٱلنَّهَارِ إِذۡ تَأۡمُرُونَنَآ أَن نَّكۡفُرَ بِٱللَّهِ وَنَجۡعَلَ لَهُۥٓ أَندَادࣰ اۚ وَأَسَرُّواْ ٱلنَّدَامَةَ لَمَّا رَأَوُاْ ٱلۡعَذَابَۚ وَجَعَلۡنَا ٱلۡأَغۡلَٰلَ فِيٓ أَعۡنَاقِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْۖ هَلۡ يُجۡزَوۡنَ إِلَّا مَا كَانُواْ يَعۡمَلُونَ
34:33.en: Those who were despised say unto those who were proud: Nay but (it was your) scheming night and day, when ye commanded us to disbelieve in Allah and set up rivals unto Him. And they are filled with remorse when they behold the doom; and We place carcans on the necks of those who disbelieved. Are they requited aught save what they used to do

14:21.ar: وَبَرَزُواْ لِلَّهِ جَمِيعࣰ ا فَقَالَ ٱلضُّعَفَٰٓؤُاْ لِلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتَكۡبَرُوٓاْ إِنَّا كُنَّا لَكُمۡ تَبَعࣰ ا فَهَلۡ أَنتُم مُّغۡنُونَ عَنَّا مِنۡ عَذَابِ ٱللَّهِ مِن شَيۡءࣲۚ قَالُواْ لَوۡ هَدَىٰنَا ٱللَّهُ لَهَدَيۡنَٰكُمۡۖ سَوَآءٌ عَلَيۡنَآ أَجَزِعۡنَآ أَمۡ صَبَرۡنَا مَا لَنَا مِن مَّحِيصࣲ‏
14:21.en: They all come forth unto their Lord. Then those who were despised say unto those who were scornful: We were unto you a following, can ye then avert from us aught of Allah's doom? They say: Had Allah guided us, we should have guided you. Whether we rage or patiently endure is (now) all one for us; we have no place of refuge

PU7lG4--Rkc.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Qalam, Part 4: Verses 17-34 Continued (the People of the Garden)
PU7lG4--Rkc.one_line: Finishing the People of the Garden: sincere generosity without judging worthiness, the stages of grief, and exalting Allah as the root of values.
PU7lG4--Rkc.summary: He completes the story of the orchard. First he humanizes the sons: to them the poor were greedy freeloaders exploiting a naive father, and he admits their case can sound persuasive. His answer is that giving for Allah's sake means no strings attached and no judging whether people deserve it, since none of us deserves what Allah gives us; giving to the ungrateful actually clarifies one's intention. Expectations should be stated openly, and favours must never be thrown back in people's faces. The Prophet gave like a man who feared no poverty. The father's legacy was sincere generosity, not land, which he illustrates with his own grandfather, still remembered by old men in his Syrian village for gifts given decades earlier. The burnt orchard was a merciful wake-up call. The sons move through denial, anger, self-blame, mutual blame and bargaining before turning to their Lord. The level-headed brother's call to glorify Allah shows that sincerity, and therefore stable values, come from truly exalting Allah. He warns that the people of the Fire pass through the same stages with no way out, and closes noting the sons repented and revived their father's generosity.

outline.heading: The surah in paragraphs: the Prophet's character, its opposites, the first story
outline.gist: The first paragraph affirms the Prophet's character, the second defines it through its opposites, and the third is the first story the Companions heard.

outline.heading: The story of the garden retold
outline.gist: A simple story that yields something new at every reading; the generous orchard owner let the needy fill their baskets on harvest morning, and his three sons did not share his outlook.

outline.heading: Humanizing the sons: the poor as greedy freeloaders
outline.gist: The Quran reports their words to humanize them, not demonize them; to them the poor were lazy, greedy and exploiting a naive father, hence 'no poor person shall enter upon you today', and he admits the case can sway his listeners.

outline.heading: Ungrateful recipients make sincerity clear
outline.gist: Shaytan despises generosity for Allah; helping the hardworking lets the intention drift toward oneself, while giving to the rude and belligerent exposes whether you give for Allah.

outline.heading: Strings attached: say so upfront, or give for Allah
outline.gist: Hoping for recognition or a return is fine if stated openly, as in buying and selling; hiding it cheats the recipient and calling it for Allah is worse; conditions like humility, self-improvement, government aid or his support of his own children are strings, and for Allah means none.

outline.heading: Giving to Allah and taking from Allah
outline.gist: Giving for Allah means never mentioning it again; the old story of a giver who said it was not for the man but for Allah, and a receiver who said he took it from Allah, not from him.

outline.heading: Judging worthiness: are you worthy of what Allah gave you?
outline.gist: The father never asked about backgrounds or what people did with it; the sons checked worthiness and were even right, but judging worthiness means it is not for Allah, since none of us deserves what Allah keeps giving despite our sins.

outline.heading: Why people withhold good: the panhandler at the light
outline.gist: The withholder of good from the surah's second paragraph withholds because he judges others unworthy, like drivers who assume the man with the cardboard sign will buy drugs; to be poor in a wealthy country is the greater tragedy, so do not judge lives you do not know.

outline.heading: Able to deprive, and they did
outline.gist: They had the power to withhold and used it; imagine arguing before Allah that you deserved His gifts and they did not; their father was not naive but understood generosity for Allah.

outline.heading: The Prophet gave like one who feared no poverty
outline.gist: A man told his people to accept Islam because Muhammad gives as one with no fear of poverty, never asking whether the taker deserves it.

outline.heading: Hunayn: you took it, so carry it yourself
outline.gist: Abu Sufyan, given a huge share of the spoils, asked for men to help carry it and was sharply told to carry it himself, a reply with a deeper meaning; the father likewise built a legacy of generosity.

outline.heading: True generosity is rare, and reminders void it
outline.gist: Sincere giving is cleansed of judgment and expectation; reminding people of favours ruins charity, and being reminded makes you want to give the gift back.

outline.heading: The real inheritance is values
outline.gist: The father reached near-perfect sincerity and the sons rushed to ruin it, so Allah took the orchard; prophets leave knowledge, not dinars, and people remember character, not possessions.

outline.heading: The old men of his village masjid in Syria
outline.gist: As a teenage imam of an old village masjid for eleven years, he served men of his grandfather's generation whose prayer was imperfect but whose faith and patience with the young taught him more than he can say.

outline.heading: His grandfather's generosity, remembered 45 years on
outline.gist: The old men kept recounting his grandfather's gifts, like the two chickens; a poor man's generosity outlived his land and became a standard for him, while the sons never saw their father's, so Allah took what they thought valuable.

outline.heading: Burnt while they slept: a merciful wake-up call
outline.gist: Asleep literally or spiritually, they needed waking, and burning the orchard was mercy; they walk the path they know and find only ash.

outline.heading: Denial: 'we must be lost'
outline.gist: The first stage of grief: they claim a wrong turn on a path they walk daily; the stages are the ego refusing to admit what happened, and he gives some cancer patients four weeks because nothing can be done until they accept the diagnosis.

outline.heading: Anger: 'rather, we are deprived'
outline.gist: Being deprived implies someone else took it, so they lash out; people who say nothing ever works out for them are simply angry; he asks Allah not to burden us beyond what we can bear.

outline.heading: The most moderate brother: why do you not glorify Allah?
outline.gist: Awsat means the most balanced, not the middle in age; he accepted at once and rebuked them, they immediately said 'exalted is our Lord, we were wrongdoers', and he asks why glorification of all things.

outline.heading: Sincerity, the root of generosity, comes from exalting Allah
outline.gist: Giving without judging, expecting or choosing recipients needs sincerity, and sincerity grows from how well you know and exalt Allah.

outline.heading: The King of kings versus feeling tired
outline.gist: How can tiredness weigh against the command of the Creator who resurrects and judges; saying this differs from internalizing it, and internalizing it is true exaltation.

outline.heading: What tasbih means and what it generates
outline.gist: Nothing resembles Allah or compares to Him and nothing is His fault; this generates sincerity, so you give to Allah and care because He commanded; Islam is His exaltation, which the sons lacked.

outline.heading: One Source, so values never change
outline.gist: Tawhid matters most because it makes the source of values one; rulings change with time but zina, theft, lying and betrayal never become acceptable, and a Muslim dropped anywhere keeps the same values.

outline.heading: Why glorification and not 'why were you not generous'
outline.gist: The values of the surah's opening depend on exalting Allah; the verses mention no shirk, yet he asks about tasbih because it is the origin of ethics; the father had it and gave from what was Allah's, the sons thought it was about money.

outline.heading: Blame: turning on one another
outline.gist: Tala'um is blame traded between parties; having rightly blamed themselves a verse earlier, their egos rebound and they point fingers at each other.

outline.heading: Bargaining: perhaps our Lord will give us better
outline.gist: Admitting they transgressed, they hope for a better garden in return, but it never came back and they lived on modest means.

outline.heading: Acceptance: to our Lord we turn in hope
outline.gist: Their last words place their hope in their Lord; it took them a while, but they reached acceptance.

outline.heading: Such is the punishment: accepting decree
outline.gist: Losing what you valued and owning your share of blame is the punishment; knowing Allah lets you accept His choice with gratitude, otherwise you accept it all the same at the end after needless torment.

outline.heading: The people of the Fire pass through the same stages
outline.gist: Told they are bound for Hell, people deny, rage, bargain and blame those who misled them, as in the Quran's dialogues of followers and leaders.

outline.heading: Acceptance there changes nothing; here there is hope
outline.gist: All five stages appear in the verses about the Fire, where patience or panic makes no difference; in this life, exalting Allah, owning the blame and changing still bring hope.

outline.heading: Repentance and gardens of bliss for the God-conscious
outline.gist: Commentators report they repented and revived their father's generosity though they stayed poor; the God-conscious get gardens of bliss for the garden they lost, and the story teaches that sincerity comes from exalting Allah.

outline.heading: Outro

68:8.en: Therefor obey not thou the rejecters

68:9.en: Who would have had thee compromise, that they may compromise

68:10.en: Neither obey thou each feeble oath-monger

68:12.en: Hinderer of the good, transgressor, malefactor

68:14.en: It is because he is possessed of wealth and children

68:15.ar: إِذَا تُتۡلَىٰ عَلَيۡهِ ءَايَٰتُنَا قَالَ أَسَٰطِيرُ ٱلۡأَوَّلِينَ
68:15.en: That, when Our revelations are recited unto him, he saith: Mere fables of the men of old

68:17.ar: إِنَّا بَلَوۡنَٰهُمۡ كَمَا بَلَوۡنَآ أَصۡحَٰبَ ٱلۡجَنَّةِ إِذۡ أَقۡسَمُواْ لَيَصۡرِمُنَّهَا مُصۡبِحِينَ
68:17.en: Lo! We have tried them as We tried the owners of the garden when they vowed that they would pluck its fruit next morning

68:18.en: And made no exception (for the Will of Allah)

68:19.ar: فَطَافَ عَلَيۡهَا طَآئِفࣱ مِّن رَّبِّكَ وَهُمۡ نَآئِمُونَ
68:19.en: Then a visitation from thy Lord came upon it while they slept

68:20.en: And in the morning it was as if plucked

68:21.en: And they cried out one unto another in the morning

68:22.ar: أَنِ ٱغۡدُواْ عَلَىٰ حَرۡثِكُمۡ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَٰرِمِينَ
68:22.en: Saying: Run unto your field if ye would pluck (the fruit)

68:23.en: So they went off, saying one unto another in low tones

68:24.ar: أَن لَّا يَدۡخُلَنَّهَا ٱلۡيَوۡمَ عَلَيۡكُم مِّسۡكِينࣱ‏
68:24.en: No needy man shall enter it to-day against you

68:25.en: They went betimes, strong in (this) purpose

68:26.en: But when they saw it, they said: Lo! we are in error

68:28.ar: قَالَ أَوۡسَطُهُمۡ أَلَمۡ أَقُل لَّكُمۡ لَوۡلَا تُسَبِّحُونَ
68:28.en: The best among them said: Said I not unto you: Why glorify ye not (Allah)

68:29.ar: قَالُواْ سُبۡحَٰنَ رَبِّنَآ إِنَّا كُنَّا ظَٰلِمِينَ
68:29.en: They said: Glorified be our Lord! Lo! we have been wrong-doers

68:30.en: Then some of them drew near unto others, self-reproaching

68:31.en: They said: Alas for us! In truth we were outrageous

68:32.ar: عَسَىٰ رَبُّنَآ أَن يُبۡدِلَنَا خَيۡرࣰ ا مِّنۡهَآ إِنَّآ إِلَىٰ رَبِّنَا رَٰغِبُونَ
68:32.en: It may be that our Lord will give us better than this in place thereof. Lo! we beseech our Lord

68:33.ar: كَذَٰلِكَ ٱلۡعَذَابُۖ وَلَعَذَابُ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ أَكۡبَرُۚ لَوۡ كَانُواْ يَعۡلَمُونَ
68:33.en: Such was the punishment. And verily the punishment of the Hereafter is greater if they did but know

68:34.ar: إِنَّ لِلۡمُتَّقِينَ عِندَ رَبِّهِمۡ جَنَّٰتِ ٱلنَّعِيمِ

7r8BFO74bN4.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Qalam, Part 3: Verses 17-34 (the People of the Garden begins)
7r8BFO74bN4.one_line: Flipping the ten traits into the Prophet's character, the arrogant dismisser of 68:14-16, and the opening of the story of the garden's owners.
7r8BFO74bN4.summary: He opens with a school survey in which most children said everything is haram, to show how few things Islam actually forbids. He then flips the ten traits of the previous verses into positive values: objectivity, integrity (distinguishing willing compromise from coercion), honesty, confidence rather than arrogance, uniting people, generosity, justice, avoiding social sin, tenderness and pride in one's identity. Identity weakness among Muslim youth worries him, and he notes the pride Gaza stirred on campuses will fade without active support. Verses 14-16 describe a man whose wealth and sons let him dismiss Allah's signs as ancient myths; he warns against reducing any person to a one-word label, a habit Muslims share. He then introduces the first story the Muslims heard in the Quran: a generous orchard owner in Yemen who let the poor take from his harvest, and his three sons who saw only land, not the legacy of generosity. He stresses that people inherit values, not wealth, and that ending an established good is a grave fault. He explains verses 17-26 in detail, ending with the sons' shocked denial at the burnt orchard as the first of the stages of grief.

outline.heading: What is haram? 'Everything,' said the children
outline.gist: In a survey of about 130 Islamic school students, 65 percent answered 'everything'. Only a few foods, drinks and relationships are forbidden; it feels like everything when society glorifies exactly those things.

outline.heading: Integrity that cannot be bought: coercion is not compromise
outline.gist: Flip the denier and you get the objective, righteous person; flip the compromiser and you get someone whose principles are not for sale, like the Prophet, who wanted nothing they offered. Doing wrong under coercion is forgiven; selling out willingly for a fee or status is not.

outline.heading: The habitual swearer flipped: honesty
outline.gist: The liar keeps swearing because he knows he has no credibility; his opposite is simply truthful.

outline.heading: Mahin flipped: confidence, not arrogance
outline.gist: The mahin feels worthless and inferior. The healthy opposite is confidence in who you are and where you come from, not arrogance or supremacy, and humility means recognising that all people are equal until Allah assigns ranks.

outline.heading: The gossip flipped: one who unites people
outline.gist: Backbiting and carrying tales divide communities and doom them to fail; the opposite is the person who brings groups together.

outline.heading: Giving, justice and avoiding social sin
outline.gist: The withholder's opposite looks for chances to distribute good; the transgressor's is just and compassionate; the athim's avoids the low behaviour society scorns, like running red lights or pushing in line.

outline.heading: Tenderness, pride in identity, and the full list of opposites
outline.gist: 'Utull's opposite is tender and kind; zanim's is proud and confident in his background. Together the ten opposites tell the Prophet, and us, what to be.

outline.heading: Muslim youth ashamed of who they are
outline.gist: Many young Muslims hide their faith and origins, Muhammad becoming Mo and Yusuf Joe; the community must push back so the next generation is proud. Gaza brought out pride on campuses, keffiyehs included, but it will fade without active support.

outline.heading: That is exactly who Muhammad was
outline.gist: He held to truth at all costs, never sold out, was honest, confident and humble, never divided people, a shepherd who learned early to gather them, never transgressed, was always tender and sure of his identity.

outline.heading: 'An kana': the particle that turns the list into one man
outline.gist: One small word shifts from the prohibitions to a person who did all of them, and why: because he had wealth and sons. Without it the verses would not make sense.

outline.heading: Wealth and sons: financial and social strength
outline.gist: Wealth is financial power and many sons a strong armed tribe; with both he felt free to dismiss what was recited to him.

outline.heading: Ayat are signs, and we take the basic ones for granted
outline.gist: Of about 120 uses of ayat in the Quran only a few mean verses; the rest are signs. You need not be a scientist to reflect on rain and seeds; people ignore recurring blessings like health and safety until they are taken away.

outline.heading: Legends of the ancients: dismissing with one word
outline.gist: Calling the signs ancient myths is how arrogance dismisses. Reducing a person with all their history and hopes to one word is deeply hurtful, yet we box people because empathising takes more energy.

outline.heading: Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, the leader who could afford to dismiss
outline.gist: Some scholars say the verses mean al-Walid, father of Khalid and one of the foremost leaders of Arabia, whose story returns in Al-Muddaththir; no one can afford to dismiss an offer of guidance.

outline.heading: Muslims do it too: the doctor called a donkey
outline.gist: Within our own circles people label one another; in the Middle East a doctor with decades of training is dismissed as an idiot in one word. This man went further and dismissed the signs of Allah himself.

outline.heading: Small faults left untamed become monsters
outline.gist: Inner faults that are not removed grow until a person can say no to the Divine, which is why the character traits just listed are the protection.

outline.heading: Branded on the snout, like the traitor's banner
outline.gist: He will be marked on the nose, the part of the face that protrudes furthest, so all can see; similarly every traitor will have a banner following him on the Day of Judgment.

outline.heading: The first story the Muslims ever heard
outline.gist: About a third of the Quran is stories, and this is the very first the Prophet and the companions heard: a simple, layered, principle-driven story fitting the surah's theme of ethics.

outline.heading: Reciting the story of the garden
outline.gist: He recites the passage through verse 34, pointing out a ten-count and a fourteen-count stretch of madd.

outline.heading: Balawnahum: we gave them an opportunity
outline.gist: Bala' here is not a test but an opportunity, like life itself; translating it as 'tested' spoils what the verse teaches.

outline.heading: Like the people of the garden: an orchard near Sana'a
outline.gist: Quraysh, granted wealth and status, were given the same opportunity as the garden's owners. Most locate it at Darwan near Sana'a in Yemen, some in Jordan; it was a large, prosperous orchard of vines, crops and fruit trees.

outline.heading: The father let the poor take first: zakat on harvests
outline.gist: On harvest morning he let the poor come in and take what they wanted before selling, which is what zakat on crops is: due on harvest day, a tenth if rain-fed or half that if irrigated. Then he died, and the story becomes one of legacy.

outline.heading: Beware of being the one who ends an established good
outline.gist: When a beautiful practice or value has been established, removing it is a grave fault; the father had established generosity toward the needy and his three sons did not see it.

outline.heading: You inherit values, not wealth
outline.gist: Inherited wealth is spent quickly; what lasts is the character and reputation parents leave. The prophets left knowledge, not money, so whoever inherits the values gets the better cut, and in a hundred years no one will remember what you owned.

outline.heading: The sons saw only land, and freeloaders where their father saw guests
outline.gist: The father stood at the gate welcoming the poor and checking they had taken from every tree. The sons saw only a farm to protect and resented the poor as freeloaders, the same arrogance that let the rich man dismiss the signs.

outline.heading: Swearing to strip it bare at dawn
outline.gist: La-yasrimunnaha: they swore to leave the garden naked, taking everything early in the morning.

outline.heading: No exceptions, but with a smile
outline.gist: They would set nothing aside, yet still wanted to protect their father's image, so rather than turn the poor away they planned to arrive before them and say they were late.

outline.heading: Ta'if: something from your Lord circled it while they slept
outline.gist: The Quran does not say whether it was a comet or anything else; it tells you only what you need, that something from Allah swept over the orchard while they slept.

outline.heading: Made truly bare: the barren land and Medina's lava fields
outline.gist: They wanted it stripped and it became truly bare; nothing has grown there since. He compares it to the black volcanic fields east and west of Medina, so deep that a dropped coin falls for seconds.

outline.heading: Calling to each other at dawn, all equally intent
outline.gist: Unlike stories with one ringleader, all the brothers were equally set on it, waking each other early to go out to their harvest.

outline.heading: An intention that survived the night
outline.gist: A bad intention made in anger and retracted after cooling down differs from theirs, which they slept on and still held at dawn; Allah knew it, hence what happened.

outline.heading: Whispering: no needy person enters today
outline.gist: Yatakhafatun is speaking so only those beside you hear. The Quran quotes their words to show the punishment was not excessive.

outline.heading: 'Ala hardin qadirin: the power to deprive was given by Allah
outline.gist: Hard is deprivation, as when a wife deprives her husband of her presence. An aside from Allah: they could withhold the orchard only because he had put it in their hands, and they chose to deprive.

outline.heading: They saw it: the stages of grief
outline.gist: Denial, anger, bargaining, depression and acceptance; whoever named the stages could have taken them from these verses, as the brothers pass through all five within hours.

outline.heading: Your core asset should be your relationship with Allah
outline.gist: Imagine the one thing whose loss would leave you with nothing. Only your relationship with Allah deserves that place; the sons had built every plan of marriage, homes and travel on the orchard.

outline.heading: 'We are lost': denial at the burnt orchard
outline.gist: Walking a path they had taken every day for decades, they found nothing and said they must have taken a wrong turn: the first stage, denial, at seeing everything they valued burnt to the ground.

H2sIG5qN1Uw.title: The Pledge of Al-Aqabah: The Fifth Article, Protecting the Message
H2sIG5qN1Uw.one_line: The Ansar's pledge to protect the Prophet was a pledge to protect the message; today its greatest threat is Muslims themselves.
H2sIG5qN1Uw.summary: The sheikh reaches the final article of the Aqabah pledge: that the Ansar protect the Prophet as they protect their families and wealth. Some treat it as specific to his time, but he argues the Prophet was not asking for personal safety. While revelation was still incomplete, he embodied the message, so protecting him meant protecting the deen, which still applies. The first four articles are incomplete without protecting and maintaining what they build. Every earlier prophetic message was corrupted over time by the hand of man, which, like a toddler, cannot leave something pure alone. Allah's promise to preserve the Quran was fulfilled through human effort, by memorizers who copied their teachers' very mouth movements, so it will not be protected any other way now. Since his audience are not policymakers, he focuses on internal threats: 3:165 tells the believers their defeat came from themselves, and a hadith says the ummah will not be destroyed from outside unless it destroys itself. Protecting Islam protects your family. In the second khutbah he tells of a wise man who promised to unveil the culprit of a city's decline and revealed a mirror, and was killed for it, as prophets were. Change began when people accepted the blame; the Prophet himself stood closest to the enemy.

outline.gist: Years 11 and 12 of prophethood have barely a page of seerah, as if cleared for the pledge. Recap: adhere in ease and hardship, commit wealth, reform values, prioritize the message. The fifth, protecting the Prophet, is often treated as historical only.

outline.heading: Protecting him was protecting the message
outline.gist: He feared nothing for himself; with revelation incomplete he was the message. Today we have the full book, and the first four articles need the fifth: keep the message from being manipulated.

outline.heading: How messages are corrupted and how the Quran was kept
outline.gist: Every prophet's teaching lost its essence to the corrupt hand of man, which like a toddler must touch anything pure. Allah's promise to preserve the Quran came true through the effort of memorizers and scholars; without that effort Islam will be lost too.

outline.heading: The internal threat: it is from yourselves
outline.gist: A surah whose halves address external and internal threats; he takes the internal. 3:165: the defeat came from you. Muslims are the biggest threat to Islam; Allah promised it will not be destroyed from outside, only if Muslims destroy one another.

outline.heading: Protect the message, protect your family
outline.gist: Islam is what protects your family, so it comes first. Fear hastening the end through our conduct: the trumpet, the angel of death taking the last lives, only Allah remaining, then the questions.

outline.heading: Which side are you on; second khutbah
outline.gist: Nothing is more valuable than the truth in that book; are we enabling its erosion or pushing back? Arabic second khutbah opening.

outline.heading: The wise man and the mirror
outline.gist: A failing city gathers to learn who is to blame; the wise man unveils a giant mirror and they kill him. It is every prophet's story: change must start with you, yet people demand someone else change.

outline.heading: Change starts within
outline.gist: When people accepted the blame, desert tribes ruled three continents within 35 years. We harm the message most by not representing it. The Prophet led every army and stood closest to the enemy. Summary of the five articles next week.
